items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Incidentally, without Jimmy Crawford do you know I never would have left Kansas City with Basie? He begged me, and here he is with Jimmy Lunceford.

ctx.x: Hey, you know who we didn't mention - Old Gal - Jimmy Crawford.

You mean the one I said, send-for to him? It's like preparing a meal. You can fix the cake but if you leave the sweetening out of it you ain't got no cake. He's the most beautiful man, you know. Naturally Mr. Lunceford had the long baton. The band's style involved itself loosely musically around Willie Smith but as a result the two-beat thing that Crawford did - you and I both knew a drummer by the name of Brown used to play at the Beale Street Theatre in Memphis. Crawford had the thing. Incidentally, without…

You remember Maxey ? He was with Cab Calloway when I joined in '36. You remember Maxey, a great drummer. I'm glad you mentioned his name. I'll tell you another guy we didn't mention yet. Of course we haven't gotten to this one fellow I'd like to say right now.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: When Eddie Tompkins, when Jabbo Smith - I said Eddie Tompkins, you know, that later went with Jimmie Lunceford

ctx.x: He's a bandleader, he had a great band.

George E. Lee, oh please. Now this is a thing that we don't go into because peoples don't know about George E. Lee. They don't know about Eli Rice. They don't know nothing about Grant Moore.
